title: Worship As Worldly Happiness First Aspect Needs Justice Sharia Prophethood And Belief

questions.question: What makes human beings different from other living things in this passage?
questions.answer: People are described as having a special nature that gives them choice, taste for beauty, and desire for a fitting life.

questions.question: Why can a person not prepare all of his needs by himself?
questions.answer: Because meeting human needs requires many different skills and jobs, and one person cannot do all of them alone.

questions.question: Why do people need to live and work together?
questions.answer: They need one another’s help and must trade the results of their work.

questions.question: Which human powers are said to have no built-in limits?
questions.answer: Desire, anger, and intellect.

questions.question: What problem comes from these powers not having fixed limits?
questions.answer: People can go too far, become unfair, and harm others.

questions.question: Why is justice needed in human society?
questions.answer: It is needed so people can deal fairly with one another when sharing and exchanging work and goods.

questions.question: Why is one person’s mind not enough to establish complete justice for everyone?
questions.answer: Because individual minds are too limited to fully understand and apply justice for all people.

questions.question: What is presented as the shared guide for justice for all people?
questions.answer: A universal law, which is the Shari‘ah.

questions.question: Why is a prophet needed after law is mentioned?
questions.answer: A prophet is needed to bring, explain, announce, and uphold that law.

questions.question: What qualities must a prophet have according to the passage?
questions.answer: He must be outstanding in character, spirit, appearance, conduct, and moral strength.

questions.question: What shows that a prophet truly has a strong connection with Allah?
questions.answer: His miracles.

questions.question: Why must belief in Allah’s greatness stay alive in people’s hearts?
questions.answer: So they will obey commands and stay away from what is forbidden.

questions.question: What keeps belief strong and fresh in people over time?
questions.answer: A repeated reminder and ongoing act, which is worship.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is worship in the end of this argument?
questions.answer: It is the regular practice that keeps belief firm and supports obedience to Allah.

questions.question: What human traits lead people to want good clothing, food, housing, and dignity?
questions.answer: Their ability to choose and their natural desire for beauty, decoration, livelihood, and a proper place in life.

questions.question: How does the passage connect human needs with arts and crafts?
questions.answer: It says proper human living depends on many kinds of skilled work.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about cooperation?
questions.answer: Human beings must help each other and exchange what they produce.

questions.question: How are humans different from animals in the way their inner powers work?
questions.answer: Animal powers have set limits, but human desire, anger, and intellect were left open.

questions.question: What is one bad result of these open-ended powers?
questions.answer: Oppression and aggression can appear among people.

questions.question: What does society need because these powers can go too far?
questions.answer: It needs justice.

questions.question: What larger source of guidance is needed beyond individual thinking?
questions.answer: A common, universal understanding in the form of law.

questions.question: What law is named as that universal measure of justice?
questions.answer: The Shari‘ah.

questions.question: Why does that law need someone to represent it?
questions.answer: Because it must be taught, declared, and enforced by an authorized messenger.

questions.question: Who fills that role of authorized messenger?
questions.answer: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: Why must the Prophet be strong in both outward and inward ways?
questions.answer: So people will accept his leadership in their minds and hearts.

questions.question: Why are miracles important in this explanation?
questions.answer: They prove that the Prophet’s mission comes from the Lord of the world.

questions.question: What is needed to make people follow commands and avoid sins?
questions.answer: A living awareness of Allah’s greatness and sovereignty.

questions.question: How is worship described in relation to belief?
questions.answer: It is the repeated act that renews belief and plants it firmly in people.

questions.question: What is the main chain of ideas in this passage from human nature to worship?
questions.answer: Human nature creates needs, needs require cooperation, cooperation requires justice, justice requires divine law, divine law requires a prophet, and lasting obedience requires worship.

questions.question: Why does human life need many kinds of work according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because people want a suitable human life, and that takes many skills to provide.

questions.question: Why can human society not function well without mutual support?
questions.answer: Because no one can produce everything needed alone.

questions.question: What three human powers are mentioned as needing control?
questions.answer: Appetite, anger, and intellect.

questions.question: What danger appears when these powers are not restrained?
questions.answer: They can cross proper limits and lead to wrongdoing.

questions.question: In this passage, what is justice supposed to protect?
questions.answer: Fair dealing among people in the exchange of effort and goods.

questions.question: Why is a universal law better than personal opinion for justice?
questions.answer: Because personal opinion is too narrow, while a shared law can guide everyone.

questions.question: What role does the Shari‘ah play in the argument?
questions.answer: It serves as the divine law that establishes justice for human society.

questions.question: Why is the Prophet necessary if the law already exists?
questions.answer: Because the law still needs a messenger to deliver it, explain it, and make it effective among people.

questions.question: What kind of excellence must the Prophet have?
questions.answer: He must be superior in body, spirit, morals, behavior, and character.

questions.question: What confirms that the Prophet is truly sent by Allah?
questions.answer: Miracles confirm his truthfulness.

questions.question: What must be strengthened in people so they will live by divine guidance?
questions.answer: The beliefs about Allah’s greatness and authority.

questions.question: Why is a repeated practice necessary for belief?
questions.answer: Because people need constant reminders for belief to stay alive and steady.

questions.question: What repeated practice does the passage identify?
questions.answer: Worship.

questions.question: Based on the whole passage, why is worship not presented as something extra?
questions.answer: Because it is shown as necessary for keeping faith strong and human life rightly guided.

questions.question: According to the passage, what special kind of life do humans naturally seek?
questions.answer: They seek a life with beauty, dignity, good provision, and a place suitable for human beings.

questions.question: What does this teach about human dependence on others?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are created to need one another’s skills and help.

questions.question: Why does the passage say trade and cooperation can become unfair?
questions.answer: Because human desires and emotions can exceed proper limits.

questions.question: Which human ability is included with desire and anger as needing limits?
questions.answer: The intellect.

questions.question: What social need rises from the risk of unfairness?
questions.answer: The need for justice.

questions.question: Why can society not rely only on separate individuals to define justice?
questions.answer: Because one person’s understanding is incomplete and cannot serve everyone fairly.

questions.question: What is meant by a universal intellect in the passage?
questions.answer: It means a shared guiding law that all people can benefit from.

questions.question: How is that shared guiding law identified?
questions.answer: It is identified as the Shari‘ah.

questions.question: What two jobs does the messenger of that law need to do?
questions.answer: He must claim and declare the law, and also uphold its authority.

questions.question: Why must people feel the Prophet’s strength in both mind and heart?
questions.answer: So his guidance remains effective outwardly and inwardly among them.

questions.question: What evidence is given for the Prophet’s relationship with Allah?
questions.answer: Miracles are given as evidence.

questions.question: What should remain present in people if they are to obey divine commands?
questions.answer: A strong sense of Allah’s majesty and rule.

questions.question: What does worship do for the truths of faith?
questions.answer: It keeps them alive, renews them, and settles them deeply in people.

questions.question: If worship were removed from this system, what would weaken first?
questions.answer: The steady remembrance of belief and the strength to obey would weaken.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human being at the start?
questions.answer: As a unique creature with a fine and unusual nature unlike other living beings.

questions.question: What desires are mentioned as part of that nature?
questions.answer: The desire to choose, to love beauty and adornment, and to seek provision and status fit for a human life.

questions.question: Why do these desires lead to a need for many professions?
questions.answer: Because proper food, clothing, and shelter require many kinds of skilled work.

questions.question: What does this show about living alone?
questions.answer: It shows that living fully alone does not match human needs.

questions.question: Why can unlimited desire, anger, and intellect become harmful?
questions.answer: Because without limits they can push people beyond justice into abuse and conflict.

questions.question: What does the passage say is needed to keep exchanges among people fair?
questions.answer: Justice is needed.

questions.question: Why is justice tied to a law for everyone rather than private thinking?
questions.answer: Because a common law can guide all people, while private thinking is not enough.

questions.question: Which law is named as that common guide?
questions.answer: The Shari‘ah.

questions.question: Why is a prophet necessary for the Shari‘ah to remain effective?
questions.answer: Because the law needs a messenger with authority to present it and preserve its force.

questions.question: What kind of person must that messenger be?
questions.answer: He must be clearly excellent in body, spirit, morals, conduct, and personality.

questions.question: What sign supports his truthfulness?
questions.answer: Miracles support it.

questions.question: What inner belief helps people follow what is commanded and leave what is forbidden?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah’s greatness and sovereignty.

questions.question: Why are reminders needed again and again?
questions.answer: Because faith must be renewed so it stays firm in people’s minds and hearts.

questions.question: What is that ongoing reminder called in the passage?
questions.answer: Worship.

questions.question: What is one big lesson of the passage about worship?
questions.answer: Worship is necessary for keeping faith active and for helping human life stay just and guided.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human nature that explains why human life is more complicated than animal life?
questions.answer: Humans have a special nature with broad desires and choices that make their needs and responsibilities greater.

questions.question: Which basic areas of life are used as examples of human needs?
questions.answer: Food, clothing, and housing.

questions.question: Why do these needs push people toward society?
questions.answer: Because people need many others’ skills and efforts to meet those needs well.

questions.question: What kind of moral problem appears when human inner powers are left without fixed limits?
questions.answer: People may become unjust and aggressive.

questions.question: What are the three inner powers named in the passage?
questions.answer: Appetite, anger, and intellect.

questions.question: What must exist when people exchange the results of their work?
questions.answer: Justice must exist.

questions.question: Why is a broad law needed for justice?
questions.answer: Because justice for all cannot rest on the limited understanding of single individuals.

questions.question: What name does the passage give to that broad divine law?
questions.answer: The Shari‘ah.

questions.question: Why is a lawgiver or messenger necessary?
questions.answer: Because the law needs someone to bring it to people, speak for it, and make it known.

questions.question: Who is identified as that messenger?
questions.answer: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: Why must the Prophet be superior in many ways?
questions.answer: So he can guide people deeply and keep influence over both their outward actions and inward states.

questions.question: What gives proof that the Prophet’s mission is from Allah?
questions.answer: Miracles give that proof.

questions.question: What belief must be kept alive so people will obey divine guidance?
questions.answer: Awareness of Allah’s greatness as the Lord and Master.

questions.question: What final need leads to worship in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: People need a repeated reminder and practice to keep faith firm.

questions.question: How is worship presented in relation to human society and faith together?
questions.answer: It supports both by keeping belief strong and helping people live under just divine guidance.
